statutory_provisions: PC Act s.7; s.13(1)(d) read with s.13(2)
evidence_type: Trap and arrest during demand and acceptance; co-accused's section 164 CrPC statement; witness examination and record scrutiny during investigation
confession: Statement of co-accused under s.164 CrPC recorded 7.8.1996; described in the background narrative only, not assessed or relied on by the Court for guilt
trial_court_outcome: Convicted by Special Judge (judgment dated 24.5.2010, as noted in amicus submission); sentence not stated
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision (Crl. M.C. No.3514 of 2008) against rejection of challenge to pardon dismissed
neutral_facts: A written complaint was made that a government official (the accused) had demanded a bribe of Rs 4,000 to settle an appeal the complainant had filed against a tax officer's order. The investigating agency laid a trap. On the day of the trap, the accused and a subordinate reader were caught while demanding and accepting the bribe from the complainant, and both were arrested. During the investigation, witnesses were examined and records scrutinised. It transpired that the subordinate had accepted the bribe money on behalf of the accused. The subordinate's statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded later. The investigating agency considered the subordinate's evidence necessary to supply missing links in a circumstantial chain that was otherwise incomplete. The subordinate was not the principal participant in the demand.
number_of_offences: 2 charged; Not stated finally upheld (Supreme Court decided only the validity of the pardon)
financial_property_loss: Rs.4,000 bribe demanded; investigation found bribe money accepted by co-accused on behalf of the accused
motive: alleged: demand of bribe to settle complainant's appeal against a Sales Tax Officer's order
trial_duration: offence: not given (complaint 29.2.1996; trap 1.3.1996); trial judgment: 24.5.2010; High Court: 6.11.2008; Supreme Court: 27.3.2014
legal_representation: Accused appeared in person; Rajiv Nanda, C.K. Sharma, B.V. Balaram Das and V. Mohana (amicus curiae) for the respondents
investigation_status: FIR/RC registered 29.2.1996; trap 1.3.1996; arrests; pardon sought during investigation before charge-sheet; charges framed 8.2.2000 after sanction; trial concluded
procedural_irregularity: Pardon granted by Metropolitan Magistrate although case was before Special Judge; Court held it a curable irregularity under s.460(g) CrPC as order was in good faith
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted by Special Judge (judgment 24.5.2010); High Court: revision dismissed 6.11.2008; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: CBI argued pardon may be moved during investigation; Magistrate exercised jurisdiction at investigation stage on Special Judge's direction; any irregularity was curable under s.460(g) CrPC
defence_argument: Magistrate lacked jurisdiction as the matter was seized before the Special Judge under s.5(2) PC Act; no hearing or notice given; challenge could be raised at any time
legal_principle_applied: During investigation the Special Judge and Magistrate have concurrent jurisdiction under s.306 CrPC; pardon after committal is not curable; pardon granted in good faith by a Magistrate is a curable irregularity under s.460(g)
precedent_relied_upon: Kanta Prashad v. Delhi Administration AIR 1958 SC 350; State of U.P. v. Kailash Nath Agarwal (1973) 1 SCC 751; A. Devendran v.
